posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
xThe Killswitch:

I haven't played DW Fixer but the idea of having to destroy stuff to deal 3 damage seems really situational.

It's pretty great actually. It takes one turn of setup, but you can start power cycling through your own weapons/styles and keep churning them out. ToolBox is the best because it nets you cards first then you can destroy it. Tons of teamates will have situational stuff out as well if they feel like helping you out. It's a pretty strong tactic and since you can search for styles you usually have a bunch. It promotes diversity of his play states where original fixer, once you find the perfect tool/style combo you pretty much don't change your board at all unless a wipe happens.

posts.name: Medic-Tank
posts.cooked:
xThe Killswitch:

It seems interesting, although it slightly goes against my playstyle to recklessly break things to do anything. I like setting up with ongoings and whatnot, and becoming a utility character. Although I guess things like Harmony would be nearly useless.And he doesn't have to destroy anything provided the board is clean anyway, right?

Darkwatch fixer is a favorite of mine as I use him after characters with risk cards like the extremely potent but dangerous hunter and hunted so chrono can do all his stuff and fixer removes the risk to do his damage. I also use him before heroes with utility cards: milking damage from a ground pound after the villain turn but before Haka is satisfying without being too damaging. And believe me if you can get jack handle, grease monkey fist and harmony other players suddenly become generous with their stuff allowing you to pretty much do the equivalent of a rampage without the drawback. Irony is Darkwatch Fixer is extremely good with standard Setback: use risk and then let fixer get your ongoings to the trash if they happened to be dangerous. If all else fails fixer has plenty of equipment and ongoings in his own deck to fuel his bitter strike.
